[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-019-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Multi Tenancy and Each Studio Deployment Plan | Studio: PlatformCore | Category: Security | Section: 1. Executive Summary | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: TenantService, PostgresRLS, QdrantTenantFilter, Neo4jScope]

AI-ConneX is designed as an industrial multi-studio platform. Multi-tenancy must therefore be implemented as a platform-wide security and data-governance property, not as a UI feature added to individual Studios. Every request, dataset, manifest, DAG, recipe, model, agent, telemetry stream, visualization, tool call, audit event and deployment must carry an authenticated tenant context and must be authorized against it.

The recommended baseline is a hybrid isolation model: shared application services with strict tenant-scoped authorization and database Row-Level Security for standard tenants; dedicated databases/namespaces/storage/keys for regulated or high-isolation tenants. This follows the principle that tenant context must be derived from verified identity, not trusted from a client-supplied header, and that isolation should exist at multiple layers. OWASP's current multi-tenant guidance explicitly calls out cross-tenant leakage, IDOR, cache/session isolation, noisy neighbors, onboarding/offboarding and audit gaps as core risks. citeturn0search1

The deployment plan uses zero-trust principles: network location is not the authorization boundary; authenticated user/service identity and resource attributes are. NIST SP 800-207 and SP 800-207A provide the architectural basis for identity-centric authorization in distributed/cloud-native systems. citeturn0search4turn0search2

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-019-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Multi Tenancy and Each Studio Deployment Plan | Studio: PlatformCore | Category: Security | Section: 2. Multi-Tenancy Definition for AI-ConneX | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: TenantService, PostgresRLS, QdrantTenantFilter, Neo4jScope]

A tenant is an independently governed industrial organization or organizational boundary whose users, data, assets, models, agents, policies and audit records must be isolated from other tenants. A tenant may contain multiple sites, plants, business units, environments and asset families.

Tenant├── Users / Groups / Service Identities├── Sites│   ├── Plants│   └── Asset Families├── Data Assets├── Manifests / DAGs / Recipes├── Features / Models├── Agents / Agent SPECs├── Knowledge Base / RAG / Graph├── Telemetry├── Tool permissions├── Deployments├── Policies├── Audit / Billing / Quotas└── Retention / Compliance settings

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-019-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Multi Tenancy and Each Studio Deployment Plan | Studio: PlatformCore | Category: Security | Section: 3. Isolation Objectives | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: TenantService, PostgresRLS, QdrantTenantFilter, Neo4jScope]

Confidentiality: Tenant A cannot read Tenant B resources.

Integrity: Tenant A cannot modify Tenant B resources.

Execution isolation: tenant-scoped jobs cannot execute against another tenant.

Knowledge isolation: RAG, graph and retrieval cannot cross tenant boundaries unless explicitly configured for shared public knowledge.

Agent isolation: Main Agents and Toolkit calls inherit tenant scope.

Telemetry isolation: live and historical industrial data remains tenant-scoped.

Cache isolation: keys always include tenant and resource scope.

Storage isolation: object paths/buckets are tenant-scoped.

Observability isolation: operators see only permitted tenant traces/logs.

Administrative isolation: platform administrators require explicit break-glass procedures for cross-tenant operations.

Offboarding: tenant data can be retained, exported and deleted according to policy.

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-019-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Multi Tenancy and Each Studio Deployment Plan | Studio: PlatformCore | Category: Security | Section: 4. R&D: Isolation Models Evaluated | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: TenantService, PostgresRLS, QdrantTenantFilter, Neo4jScope]

PostgreSQL RLS should be treated as defense in depth rather than the only control. OWASP recommends database-level isolation plus application/data-access authorization, tenant-scoped composite lookups, cache/storage isolation and per-tenant quotas. citeturn0search1

| Model | Isolation | Cost | Recommended use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Shared DB + tenant_id | Medium | Low | Prototype / very high tenant count |
| Shared DB + PostgreSQL RLS | High when correctly implemented | Low/Medium | Default SaaS tier |
| Schema per tenant | High | Medium | Enterprise tier |
| DB per tenant | Very high | High | Regulated/high-value tenants |
| Dedicated namespace + storage + DB | Very high | High | Premium/regulated |
| Hybrid | Variable | Variable | AI-ConneX recommended |

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-019-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Multi Tenancy and Each Studio Deployment Plan | Studio: PlatformCore | Category: Security | Section: 5. Recommended AI-ConneX Tenancy Tiers | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: TenantService, PostgresRLS, QdrantTenantFilter, Neo4jScope]

The tier is a deployment policy. It should not change the application authorization contract: every service still receives and validates tenant context.

| Tier | Isolation design | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| T1 Shared | Shared services + RLS + scoped storage | SME / pilot |
| T2 Enterprise | RLS + dedicated schema/storage + dedicated keys | Industrial group |
| T3 Regulated | Dedicated DB/namespace + keys + isolated workloads | High-compliance site |
| T4 Sovereign/Private | Dedicated cluster or on-prem deployment | Critical infrastructure / private cloud |

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-019-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Multi Tenancy and Each Studio Deployment Plan | Studio: PlatformCore | Category: Security | Section: 6. Tenant Context | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: TenantService, PostgresRLS, QdrantTenantFilter, Neo4jScope]

{  "tenant_uid": "TEN-7f8...",  "org_uid": "ORG-...",  "user_uid": "USR-...",  "roles": ["TENANT_ADMIN"],  "site_scope": ["SITE-01"],  "asset_scope": ["COMP-*"],  "environment": "prod",  "policy_version": "POL-12"}

Tenant context is generated from a verified identity/token and server-side membership lookup. A client may request a site or tenant, but the server determines whether the authenticated principal has that scope. OWASP specifically recommends deriving tenant context from authenticated sessions and not trusting client-supplied tenant IDs. citeturn0search1

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-019-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Multi Tenancy and Each Studio Deployment Plan | Studio: PlatformCore | Category: Security | Section: 7. Authorization Model | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: TenantService, PostgresRLS, QdrantTenantFilter, Neo4jScope]

AI-ConneX should combine RBAC with ABAC/ReBAC-style attributes. Role answers 'what class of operation?', while attributes answer 'on which tenant/site/asset/environment?'. OWASP notes that ABAC can better represent multi-organizational access patterns than role-only designs. citeturn0search0

ALLOW if:identity.validAND identity.activeAND tenant_membership(identity, tenant)AND resource.tenant_uid == tenant.uidAND site in identity.site_scopeAND asset in identity.asset_scopeAND action in role.permissionsAND policy.allows(action, resource, context)

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-019-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Multi Tenancy and Each Studio Deployment Plan | Studio: PlatformCore | Category: Security | Section: 8. Defense-in-Depth Isolation | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: TenantService, PostgresRLS, QdrantTenantFilter, Neo4jScope]

CLIENT  |API Gateway / WAF  |  authenticate  vTenant Context Middleware  |Authorization / Policy  |Service-to-Service Identity  |Repository / Query Scope  |Database RLS  |Storage / Cache / Queue Scope  |Audit + Monitoring

The decisive authorization check is server-side. UI filtering is only a usability feature. OWASP's authorization guidance explicitly recommends server-side enforcement, deny-by-default and authorization tests. citeturn0search0

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-019-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Multi Tenancy and Each Studio Deployment Plan | Studio: PlatformCore | Category: Security | Section: 9. Database Design | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: TenantService, PostgresRLS, QdrantTenantFilter, Neo4jScope]

CREATE TABLE datasets (  dataset_uid UUID PRIMARY KEY,  tenant_uid UUID NOT NULL,  site_uid UUID,  name TEXT NOT NULL,  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL);ALTER TABLE datasets ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;CREATE POLICY tenant_dataset_policyON datasetsUSING (tenant_uid = current_setting('app.current_tenant')::uuid)WITH CHECK (tenant_uid = current_setting('app.current_tenant')::uuid);CREATE INDEX idx_dataset_tenantON datasets(tenant_uid, dataset_uid);

Every tenant-scoped table should have tenant_uid. For high-value objects, use composite uniqueness such as (tenant_uid, object_uid) or UUIDs with server-side ownership checks.

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-019-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Multi Tenancy and Each Studio Deployment Plan | Studio: PlatformCore | Category: Security | Section: 10. Object Storage Isolation | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: TenantService, PostgresRLS, QdrantTenantFilter, Neo4jScope]

s3://aconnext/{tenant_uid}/{site_uid}/{studio}/{resource_type}/{resource_uid}/...Examples:TEN-01/SITE-01/data/compiler/DATASET-001/TEN-01/SITE-01/data/profiler/MANIFEST-001/TEN-01/SITE-01/ml/model/MODEL-007/TEN-01/SITE-01/agent/evidence/EXEC-009/

Bucket/container policy denies cross-tenant prefixes.

Signed URLs are short-lived and scope-limited.

Object metadata stores tenant_uid.

Deletion jobs verify tenant ownership.

Encryption keys can be tenant-specific for higher tiers.

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-019-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Multi Tenancy and Each Studio Deployment Plan | Studio: PlatformCore | Category: Security | Section: 11. Cache / Queue / Vector / Graph Isolation | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: TenantService, PostgresRLS, QdrantTenantFilter, Neo4jScope]

CACHE KEYtenant:{tenant_uid}:site:{site_uid}:resource:{resource_uid}QUEUEtopic:tenant.{tenant_uid}.eventsVECTOR FILTERtenant_uid == authenticated_tenantGRAPHMATCH (n {tenant_uid: $tenant_uid})...TELEMETRYWHERE tenant_uid = $tenant_uid

Shared caches, vector stores and graphs are frequent sources of accidental cross-tenant exposure. Tenant scope must be applied before retrieval/query execution, not after results are returned.

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-019-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Multi Tenancy and Each Studio Deployment Plan | Studio: PlatformCore | Category: Security | Section: 12. Multi-Tenant Identity | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: TenantService, PostgresRLS, QdrantTenantFilter, Neo4jScope]

Service identities must carry tenant context just like humans. 'Internal service' is not an authorization exemption.

| Identity | Scope |
| --- | --- |
| Platform operator | Explicitly granted platform functions; no automatic tenant-data access |
| Tenant admin | One tenant |
| Site admin | Tenant + selected sites |
| Engineer | Tenant + assigned assets/sites |
| Operator | Tenant + operational assets |
| Agent service identity | Tenant + SPEC-defined site/asset scope |
| Tool service identity | Tenant + capability scope |
| Pipeline worker | Tenant + job/resource scope |

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-019-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Multi Tenancy and Each Studio Deployment Plan | Studio: PlatformCore | Category: Security | Section: 13. Tenant Provisioning Flow | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: TenantService, PostgresRLS, QdrantTenantFilter, Neo4jScope]

CREATE TENANT -> validate organization -> allocate tenant UID -> create policy -> provision storage -> provision DB schema/RLS context -> create encryption key reference -> create default roles -> create quotas -> create audit stream -> create isolated namespace if tier requires -> create initial admin -> run isolation tests -> ACTIVATE

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-019-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Multi Tenancy and Each Studio Deployment Plan | Studio: PlatformCore | Category: Security | Section: 14. Tenant Offboarding | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: TenantService, PostgresRLS, QdrantTenantFilter, Neo4jScope]

Freeze new workloads.

Revoke user/service credentials.

Stop scheduled agents and pipelines.

Export data if contract/policy requires.

Retain required audit/legal records.

Delete or cryptographically erase tenant data according to retention policy.

Remove vector/graph/cache entries.

Remove object storage.

Delete dedicated namespace/database if applicable.

Run cross-tenant deletion verification.

Produce signed offboarding report.

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-019-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Multi Tenancy and Each Studio Deployment Plan | Studio: PlatformCore | Category: Security | Section: 15. Tenant-Aware AI-ConneX Pipeline | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: TenantService, PostgresRLS, QdrantTenantFilter, Neo4jScope]

JANE  -> Intent {tenant_uid, user_uid, site_scope}  -> COMPILER  -> PROFILER  -> DAG ASSIGNER  -> RECIPE ORCHESTRATOR  -> PREPARE  -> FEATURE ENGINEER  -> IF/ELSE      |-> DATA STUDIO DEPLOYMENT      |-> ML STUDIO             -> STEM             -> MODEL             -> AGENTIC STUDIO  -> VISUALIZER / AGENT / TOOLKIT  -> AUDIT

At every transition, the output contract carries tenant_uid and scope. The downstream stage rejects missing, invalid or mismatched tenancy.

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-019-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Multi Tenancy and Each Studio Deployment Plan | Studio: PlatformCore | Category: Security | Section: 20. Studio 2 — Data Studio Deployment | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: TenantService, PostgresRLS, QdrantTenantFilter, Neo4jScope]

Data Studio contains Compiler, Profiler, DAG Assigner, Recipe Orchestrator, Prepare, Feature Engineer and the deployment conditional.

Gateway -> Data API -> Compiler workers -> Profiler workers -> DAG service -> Recipe service -> Prepare/FE workers -> Artifact/Object Storage -> Manifest Registry -> Data Studio Deployment Node

Use queue-backed workers for large datasets.

Use tenant-scoped object storage paths.

Attach tenant_uid to every manifest, family ID and DAG ID.

Use resource quotas per tenant to prevent noisy-neighbor failures.

Use ephemeral workers for untrusted uploaded files.

Scan archives before extraction.

Keep lineage from chatbot intent to manifest UID.

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-019-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Multi Tenancy and Each Studio Deployment Plan | Studio: PlatformCore | Category: Security | Section: 21. Studio 3 — ML Studio Deployment | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: TenantService, PostgresRLS, QdrantTenantFilter, Neo4jScope]

ML Studio consumes Data Studio artifacts or a new cleaned/prepared dataset, then runs the STEM loop: Split → Train → Evaluate Metrics → Judge/Score.

Gateway -> ML API -> Dataset/Manifest Resolver -> STEM Orchestrator -> Parallel Model Workers -> Evaluation Service -> Judge/Scorer -> Model Registry -> Inference Endpoint -> Agentic Studio (if requested)

Model runs inherit tenant and dataset scope.

Feature artifacts are tenant-scoped.

Model registry records tenant ownership.

Model endpoints enforce tenant authorization.

GPU/CPU quotas prevent noisy-neighbor exhaustion.

Training data and artifacts are encrypted and versioned.

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-019-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Multi Tenancy and Each Studio Deployment Plan | Studio: PlatformCore | Category: Security | Section: 22. Studio 4 — Agentic Studio Deployment | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: TenantService, PostgresRLS, QdrantTenantFilter, Neo4jScope]

Agentic Studio is the highest-risk Studio because it can coordinate tools and persistent operational workflows. Its tenant boundary must exist at Agent SPEC, Runtime, knowledge retrieval, toolkit gateway and audit layers.

Gateway -> Agent Builder -> Agent SPEC Registry -> Agent Runtime -> Knowledge Foundation    -> RAG    -> Knowledge Graph    -> Knowledge Base    -> Telemetry    -> Models -> Policy Engine -> Toolkit Registry -> Tool Gateway -> Industrial/Business Connectors -> Audit / Visualizer

Agent UID is tenant-scoped.

SPEC cannot reference a tool outside tenant policy.

RAG filters before retrieval.

Graph queries include tenant scope.

Telemetry queries include tenant/site scope.

Toolkit calls inherit execution scope.

Approval requests are tenant-bound.

Audit records include tenant UID.

[Governed Subsystems: TenantService, PostgresRLS, QdrantTenantFilter, Neo4jScope]

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-019-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Multi Tenancy and Each Studio Deployment Plan | Studio: PlatformCore | Category: Security | Section: 47. Conclusion | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: TenantService, PostgresRLS, QdrantTenantFilter, Neo4jScope]

Multi-tenancy is the platform foundation that makes AI-ConneX suitable for multiple industrial organizations. The key architectural decision is not merely 'add tenant_id'; it is to propagate authenticated tenant context through the entire lifecycle—from Jane's intent, through Data Studio's artifacts and ML Studio's models, into Agentic Studio's SPEC/runtime/knowledge/toolkit, and finally into every operational action and audit record.

The recommended implementation combines application authorization, database isolation, storage/cache/vector/graph/telemetry scoping, service identity, network controls, quotas, auditability and continuous cross-tenant testing. This defense-in-depth model aligns with current OWASP multi-tenant guidance and NIST zero-trust principles. citeturn0search1turn0search2
